# config.toml settings

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_config_docs.py from
src/wgsextract_cli/core/settings_schema.py; run `just regen`. -->

WGS Extract reads its settings from config.toml: `wgsextract config` prints where it is and every setting's value, and `--config PATH` picks another file for one run. Command-line options override settings for a run.

config.toml lives in the users workspace, `~/wgs-extract` (`%USERPROFILE%\wgs-extract` on Windows), beside the default My Genomes library (`mygenomes/`): the folders you manage and may want on another disk. An install that already keeps config.toml where earlier versions did (the per-user config folder, `~/.config/wgsextract` on macOS) keeps using it. Reference data, reference genomes and temporary files stay in the CLI's own data folder unless config.toml names other folders. The WGS Extract desktop app keeps its settings in the same folder, so the two share them.

If both a legacy CLI config and a users-workspace config exist, the CLI keeps using the legacy file and warns with both paths. Use `--config PATH` to select the other explicitly. Opening the desktop app does not change this precedence or erase saved advanced settings.

Without output_directory, a command writes to a `wgse/` folder beside its input from the lab (a BAM or CRAM, else FASTQs, else a VCF, else a raw microarray file), or beside an input already in a `wgse/` folder. The folder of the lab's original files stays untouched: only indexes that must sit beside their files are written there, and writing a BAM, CRAM, FASTQ, VCF or microarray file into it warns (`primary_overwrite`).

Every value is checked when the file loads: a value of the wrong type, outside its range or not one of its choices stops the run with an error that names the setting and what it expects. An unknown setting is ignored with a warning that suggests the closest name.

<!-- Usage guide: edit docs/data/configuration-guide.md, then regenerate. -->
## Choosing and editing a config

`--config FILE` works anywhere on the command line and selects the file for
both reading and saving, before validation. An invalid unused default cannot
block a valid alternate file; a bundling tool can choose a separate config.
The CLI and desktop app otherwise share the users-workspace config described
above. Former per-user locations, still recognized for existing installs, are:

- macOS: `~/.config/wgsextract/config.toml` if that file exists, otherwise
  `~/Library/Application Support/wgsextract/config.toml` if present;
- Linux: `~/.config/wgsextract/config.toml`;
- Windows: `%LocalAppData%\theontho\wgsextract\config.toml`.

Saves are atomic; `wgsextract config` prompts only in an interactive terminal.
A save from the CLI or the desktop app waits while another is in progress,
holding a hidden `.config.toml.lock` beside the file, and keeps the other's
changes; after 60 seconds it fails, naming the lock.
If the selected file contains invalid TOML or is not UTF-8, the CLI stops and
reports the file path and error location. Correct the file or select a valid
one with `--config`.
Boolean values must be unquoted `true`/`false`, never `"false"`.
Threads accept a positive integer or `"auto"`; legacy numeric strings such
as `"4"` still work. Integer thresholds/TTLs require integers, not quoted
numbers or booleans. Memory (`"2G"`), paths and image names are strings;
`vcf_input_paths`/`server_allowed_paths` also accept string arrays.
Ports, job counts and thresholds must be in range; choice settings
(`server_mcp_transport`, `microarray_quirks`, `native_aligners`) must match
their listed choices. Aliases obey the same rules as canonical keys.

Invalid configured thread counts warn and use automatic threads, unless
explicit `--threads` overrides them; saves still require a valid count.
Other invalid types stop startup with one concise line naming key, file and
expected type. There is no `config set` or `config show` repair command:
edit the file, or choose a valid `--config PATH`, before rerunning even help
or `config`. Missing-setting defaults and valid values are unchanged.

## Example

```toml
# Defaults for --input and --outdir
input = "/data/genomes/joe/joe.cram"
outdir = "/data/wgse-out"

# FASTA (--ref); reference library; reference genomes only
ref = "/data/reference/genomes/hs38.fa.gz"
reflib = "/data/reference"
reference_genome_library = "/data/reference/genomes"

# One folder per person/sample, selected by --genome
dataset_library = "/data/datasets"

threads = "auto"  # Apple Silicon per-stage core plan; all cores elsewhere
memory = "auto"   # sort memory per thread; see hardware guide

# Optional external-tool overrides (otherwise use PATH)
haplogrep_path = "/path/to/haplogrep3"
haplogrep_tree = "phylotree-fu-rcrs"  # or phylotree-rcrs, mitotree-rcrs
y_tree = "yfull"                    # or yfull_v10, ftdna, isogg, [y_trees] id
vep_cache = "~/.vep"
```

Short keys are aliases: `wgsextract config` displays `input_path`,
`output_directory`, `reference_fasta`, `reference_library`, `cpu_threads`,
`memory_limit` and the other canonical names. Either spelling works;
explicit command-line options win for that run. Other settings include
annotation paths (`clinvar_vcf_path`, `gnomad_vcf_path`, `gnomad_sv_path`,
`gnomad_lr_sv_path`, `revel_tsv_path`, …), `mother_vcf`/`father_vcf`, and
the `[dev]` settings below.

By default the reference library is `reference/` in the app data folder;
reference genomes are its `genomes/`. A `--ref` FASTA chooses sequence.
When it is in the configured library's `reference_genome_library` (else
`genomes/`), that library supplies other assets. Only genomes and their derived
files go there; datasets belong in `dataset_library`. Otherwise the FASTA's
folder is searched first, then configured `reference_library`, for chains,
ploidy files, chip templates and annotations. Missing-file errors name the
searched folders. See [dataset discovery and example genomes](sample-workspace.md#dataset-library).

For resource defaults, `memory = "auto"` uses up to 25% of effective RAM
(including Linux cgroup v2 limits) split across threads; `"2G"` sets a
per-thread budget, still subject to the sort caps. See
[threads and memory](hardware.md#threads-and-memory) rather than treating it
as a whole-pipeline RAM cap.

## Temporary files and atomic outputs

Set `temp_directory = "/data/scratch"` or pass `--tmp-dir DIRECTORY` for
samtools/sambamba sort spills, GATK temp files and realign staging.
It must exist and be writable. Each run owns a workspace, normally removed
on success/failure; final files stay in `--outdir`. If realign fails after
extracting FASTQs, it retains the workspace and prints `--r1`/`--r2` reuse
paths; remove it after recovery. `--keep-fastq` instead keeps extracted reads
in the output directory. Unset defaults/tool arguments are unchanged.
Native pbmm2's sorter cannot honor this option: omit it or use minimap2.
This controls placement/capacity, not promised speed.

BWA/bwa-mem2 indexes require all nonempty index files, build under an exclusive
lock with a staged prefix, and rebuild after interruption rather than trusting
partial files. See [hardware-specific index requirements](hardware.md#cpu-aligners)
for native versions that do not need `.0123`.

`align` always validates and publishes atomically, even with `--no-atomic-output`,
so validation failure preserves previous alignments. `vcf to-fasta` also stages
its FASTA, indexes, and requested chain beside their destinations; if generation
or indexing fails, the previous files are unchanged. A hidden lock file stays
in the output directory so concurrent retries cannot mix results.
`--atomic-output` (or
`atomic_outputs = true`) opts realign, SNP/InDel/GATK/FreeBayes callers and
main extract writers into rename publication, with indexes generated afterward.
Failed writes preserve previous files. Other commands keep the opt-in default:
staged paths alter tool provenance headers and can need extra disk.
`--no-atomic-output` disables their configured opt-in, not alignment or consensus
safety.
This adds no resume/skip behaviour; see [step journals](step-resume.md).

## Keep-awake

`--keep-awake` or `keep_awake = true` requests idle/sleep inhibition until
exit. `--no-keep-awake` overrides config, including delegated analyze,
annotation-chain and benchmark commands; `keep_awake = false` is the default.
macOS uses `caffeinate`, Linux uses already-installed/permitted
`systemd-inhibit`, and native Windows uses `SetThreadExecutionState`.
Missing helpers, denied permissions or cleanup errors never fail the run.
This prevents automatic sleep, not shutdown or forced/manual suspension;
display sleep is allowed. Report-only help/config/deps never inhibit sleep.

## Settings

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_reference_downloads` | boolean | `false` | Allow first-use public reference/model downloads for commands with --download (hosts and request data: docs/privacy.md); no sample uploads |
| `input_path` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Default input BAM/CRAM or FASTQ file |
| `output_directory` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Default output directory (default: wgse/ beside the primary input BAM, CRAM, FASTQ, VCF or microarray file, or that folder if already wgse/) |
| `temp_directory` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Temporary Workload directory: every command's temporary work (sort spills, staging, scratch files) |
| `atomic_outputs` | boolean | `false` | Publish completed main outputs by rename (changes tool provenance paths) |
| `reference_fasta` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to the reference genome FASTA |
| `reference_library` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Reference data directory (annotation data, gene maps, VEP caches) |
| `reference_genome_library` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Folder holding only the reference genomes (FASTAs) and the files made from them, for reference_library (default: genomes/ in it) |
| `mygenomes_library` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | My Genomes library: one folder per person or sample (default: mygenomes/ in the users workspace; formerly dataset_library) |
| `cpu_threads` | integer or `auto` | `"auto"` | CPU threads: a positive integer for every stage, or auto (per-stage core-layout plan on Apple Silicon; all cores elsewhere) |
| `memory_limit` | string | `"auto"` | Memory limit per thread, e.g. 2G (auto: 25% of RAM split across threads) |
| `debug_mode` | boolean | `false` | Enable verbose debug logging |
| `quiet_mode` | boolean | `false` | Enable quiet mode (errors only) |
| `log_dir` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Opt-in directory for unique persistent DEBUG run logs and provenance; it keeps the newest 100 runs |
| `state_directory` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Folder for the last-run record and saved bug reports (report-issue); default: state/ in the data folder |
| `server_port` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `0` | Default HTTP/JSON listen port (0: any free port); an embedded server.listen port overrides this default, and explicit --port wins |
| `server_allowed_paths` | string or array of strings, path (`~` expands) | unset | Folders (a string or an array) `wgsextract serve` requests may read and write, besides mygenomes_library, reference_library, reference_genome_library and output_directory |
| `server_mcp_transport` | `stdio` or `http` | `"stdio"` | How `wgsextract serve --mcp` speaks MCP: stdio, or http (streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1 with a per-launch token; needs the optional 'mcp' package) |
| `server_mcp_port` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `0` | Port `wgsextract serve --mcp-transport http` listens on at 127.0.0.1 (0: any free port) |
| `server_max_jobs` | integer, at least 1 | `1` | Long `wgsextract serve` jobs that run at once; more wait in a queue |
| `keep_awake` | boolean | `false` | Best-effort sleep inhibition while commands run (opt-in) |
| `result_card` | boolean | `false` | Also write `<name>.card.html`, a shareable page of each run's result, beside its manifest |
| `haplogrep_executable` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to the Haplogrep 3 executable or JAR |
| `dorado_executable` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to ONT's dorado executable for `basecall` |
| `discvrseq_jar` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to DISCVRseq.jar for `vcf variantqc` |
| `java17_executable` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to a Java 17 binary for tools requiring Java 17 (such as `vcf variantqc`) |
| `granite_executable` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to the granite executable for `vcf granite-qc` |
| `native_aligners` | `auto` or `off` | unset | Apple Silicon: `align`/`realign` use wgse-bwa, wgse-bwa-mem2, wgse-bwa-mem3 and wgse-minimap2 when on PATH (auto, the default) or never (off); Linux: Bioconda's bwa-mem3 in place of bwa/bwa-mem2; Windows x86-64: use wgse-bwa and wgse-minimap2 when installed |
| `wgse_bwa_path` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to an optional native Windows x86-64 wgse-bwa executable |
| `output_profile` | `default` or `archive` or `calling` | `"default"` | `align`/`realign`: default keeps --format; archive selects lossless CRAM 3.1 (GATK 4.7+); calling selects compatible CRAM 3.0 |
| `prefer_native_gpu` | boolean | unset | `align`/`realign`: on Windows, native CUDA is automatic when it fits; set false to force CPU. Elsewhere, set true to prefer wgse-bwa's native GPU even above the RAM budget after normal sort step-down; retain explicit memory, otherwise cap default/config sort at 256M (may swap heavily) |
| `dense_suffix_array` | boolean | `false` | `align`/`realign`: wgse-bwa reads the reference's dense suffix-array file from `ref dense-sa` (opt-in; used only when wgse-bwa aligns; holds it in RAM, 0.8 GB for hs38) |
| `dorado_models_directory` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Folder `basecall` downloads Dorado models into (default: the wgsextract cache's dorado-models) |
| `mimalloc` | `auto` or `off` | unset | Apple Silicon: `vcf snp`/`vcf indel` run bcftools with WGS Extract's wgse-mimalloc allocator. Native Windows: `bam to-cram --cram-version 3.1` with a local reference uses the matching samtools-mimalloc encoder. Only validated installed variants run (auto, default), or never (off) |
| `baq` | boolean | `false` | `vcf snp`/`vcf indel`: enable heuristic base alignment quality (BAQ) in bcftools mpileup (slower; may reduce low-depth recall); off by default; see docs/variant-confidence.md |
| `reference_evidence` | `none` or `gvcf` | `"none"` | `vcf snp`/`vcf indel`/`vcf deepvariant`/`vcf gatk`/`vcf clair3`: also write a gVCF of reference evidence (bcftools.g.vcf.gz, deepvariant.g.vcf.gz, gatk.g.vcf.gz, clair3.g.vcf.gz) beside the variant VCF (gvcf), or not (none, the default); see docs/reference-evidence.md |
| `haplocheck_executable` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to the haplocheck executable or JAR |
| `report_gene_list` | string | unset | `report`: genes of the ClinVar section, a built-in list (acmg-sf-3.3, the default, or acmg-sf-3.2) or a TSV or BED file |
| `haplogrep_tree` | string | unset | Haplogrep 3 tree for mtDNA haplogroups: phylotree-fu-rcrs (default), phylotree-rcrs or mitotree-rcrs |
| `y_tree` | string | unset | Y haplogroup tree for `lineage y-haplogroup`: yfull (default), yfull_v10, ftdna, isogg or a [y_trees] id |
| `y_trees` | tables | unset | Your own Y haplogroup trees, one [y_trees.<id>] table each (see the Yleaf README) |
| `jar_directory` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Directory for JAR tools |
| `vep_cache_directory` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to VEP cache |
| `vep_engine` | `vep-rs` or `ensembl` | unset | Engine `vep run` annotates with: vep-rs (default) or ensembl |
| `pharmcat_directory` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Extracted PharmCAT pipeline release |
| `parabricks_image` | string | unset | NVIDIA Parabricks Docker image for GPU alignment and calling (default nvcr.io/nvidia/clara/clara-parabricks:4.8.0-1) |

| `deepvariant_native` | `auto` or `off` | unset | `vcf deepvariant` runs wgse-deepvariant (Apple Silicon, Linux x86-64) when it is on PATH (auto, the default) or never (off) |
| `deepvariant_weights` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Folder of the weights wgse-deepvariant calls with (from its macos-deepvariant or linux-deepvariant release) |

| `methylation_context` | `cpg` or `all` | `"cpg"` | `methylation pileup` context: cpg (CpG sites) or all (every cytosine) |

| `microarray_assume_hom_ref` | boolean | `false` | Treat absent VCF markers on represented contigs as homozygous reference |
| `microarray_exclude_filtered` | boolean | `true` | Write microarray no-calls for VCF FILTER values other than PASS or . |
| `microarray_call_reasons` | boolean | `false` | Write a companion CombinedKit_reasons.tsv with explicit call/no-call reasons |

## The [server] table

Operator opt-ins for HTTP/JSON listening and viewer files. See [server mode](server.md#remote-http-access) for exposure and TLS requirements.

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `listen` | string | `"127.0.0.1"` | HTTP listen address[:port]; explicit --port overrides the embedded port; loopback by default |
| `allowed_hosts` | string or array of strings | unset | Exact external Host headers, including ports; never wildcards |
| `allowed_origins` | string or array of strings | unset | Exact app origins allowed to read viewer files; never wildcards |
| `viewer_files` | boolean | `false` | Enable authenticated, guarded viewer byte ranges |
| `public_url` | string | unset | Advertised HTTP/HTTPS client origin; required for non-loopback listening, with its authority in allowed_hosts |
| `max_connections` | integer, 1 to 256 | `32` | Maximum accepted HTTP connections, including unauthenticated peers |
| `header_timeout_seconds` | number, 0.1 to 60 | `10.0` | Absolute request-header and keep-alive idle deadline; does not limit authenticated responses |

## The [dev] table

Developer and test settings live in their own table, at the end of config.toml (after a table header, every key belongs to that table):

```toml
[dev]
download_cache = true
```

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pet_r1_fastq` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to PET R1 reads |
| `pet_r2_fastq` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to PET R2 reads |
| `pet_reference_fasta` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to PET reference genome |
| `real_genome_test_path` | string, path (`~` expands) | unset | Path to a local real genome dataset |
| `real_genome_tests_enabled` | boolean | `false` | Enable real smoke tests from real_genome_test_path |
| `download_cache` | boolean | `false` | Cache downloads under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/wgsextract for reuse |
| `download_cache_ttl_seconds` | integer, at least 0 | `604800` | Seconds before an unused download cache item is pruned |

These used to be top-level settings; a config.toml that still has one there fails to load, naming its place in [dev]: `dev_download_cache` (now `download_cache`), `dev_download_cache_ttl_seconds` (now `download_cache_ttl_seconds`), `pet_r1_fastq` (now `pet_r1_fastq`), `pet_r2_fastq` (now `pet_r2_fastq`), `pet_reference_fasta` (now `pet_reference_fasta`), `real_genome_test_path` (now `real_genome_test_path`), `real_genome_tests_enabled` (now `real_genome_tests_enabled`).
